findings.title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import stores attacker-controlled RSS/Atom or scraped page contents as a Post with cook_method raw_html. Post#cook returns raw verbatim for that method, and the cooked HTML is rendered raw in topic and embed views. No sanitization is applied on this path (PollFeed passes feed content straight through), so a feed item or embedded page containing <script>/event-handler markup becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor who views the imported topic.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
findings.body: i.content is nil for RSS/Atom items that only provide a summary/description (SimpleRSS does not guarantee content), so i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole hourly poll, preventing all remaining items from being imported. String#scrub also does not exist on the Ruby 1.9/2.0 runtimes this codebase targets, so this raises NoMethodError even when content is present.

findings.title: Unescaped referer is interpolated into inline JavaScript
findings.body: request.referer is inserted verbatim inside a single-quoted JS string passed to postMessage. The controller only checks the referer's host, so a referer such as http://<embeddable_host>/'-alert(1)-' contains a quote that breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. The referer must be JS/HTML-escaped (and reduced to an origin) before interpolation.

findings.title: Full referer URL used as postMessage targetOrigin never matches
findings.body: postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but this passes the entire request.referer including its path and query. Browsers compare it against the parent window's origin, so the discourse-resize message is silently never delivered and the embed iframe added by embed.js never gets resized to its content height.

findings.title: Unauthenticated requests can flood the retrieve_topic job queue
findings.body: Every GET for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job. The 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever#retrieve, which only runs when a job is executed, not before enqueueing. Anyone who can present the embeddable referer can therefore issue many requests for distinct or identical URLs faster than jobs drain and fill Sidekiq with jobs that each may fetch remote pages/feed content, instead of throttling/deduplicating at enqueue time.

findings.title: Spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever use that the controller no longer performs
findings.body: This test expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve to be called during EmbedController#best, but the controller instead calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). The mock expectations can never be satisfied by the implementation under test, so this example fails and provides no coverage of the actual enqueued job arguments (user_id and embed_url).

findings.title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with no validation
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url) on the supplied URL before TopicEmbed.import's scheme check runs, and performs no host allowlist, private-address, or redirect validation. Callers that pass externally influenced URLs (e.g. thread links from a Disqus export) can make the server issue requests to internal/metadata addresses (SSRF) and import the response. Host validation in TopicRetriever does not protect this entry point.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of origin equality
findings.body: The handler accepts a message whenever discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1, i.e. whenever the sender's origin is any substring of the configured Discourse URL, rather than requiring e.origin to equal the Discourse origin. Origins that are prefixes/substrings of the configured URL are accepted, weakening the check that the resize message actually came from the Discourse embed iframe; the origin should be parsed once and compared exactly.
